exp/e: The number e is about two point seven one eight, written e is about two point seven one eight: the wavy equals sign means “is about”. e to the x means e multiplied by itself, x times.
exp/zero: e to the zero is one. Each step of one in x multiplies by e again: two point seven two, seven point three nine, then about twenty.
exp/neg: A step down divides by e instead: e to the minus one is zero point three seven. Smaller, but never negative. e to any power is positive.
exp/add: So adding powers multiplies results. e squared times e to the one is e cubed, where the raised dot means times: the powers add, two plus one.
exp/div: Dividing takes factors of e away. e cubed over e to the one is e squared: twenty point oh nine divided by two point seven two is seven point three nine. The powers subtract, three minus one.
exp/pow: And e squared, cubed is e squared times itself three times. The powers add, two plus two plus two, which is three times two: e to the six. A power of a power multiplies.
log/ask: The natural log, ln, runs this backwards. For a positive number y, ln of y asks: e to what power gives y?
log/two: e squared is seven point three nine, so ln of seven point three nine is two.
log/one: e to the zero is one, so ln of one is zero.
log/neg: Below one, the log is negative: ln of zero point three seven is minus one. Any number between zero and one has a negative log.
log/undo: ln and e to the x undo each other. For any number a, ln of e to the a is a, and for a positive a, e to the ln of a is a.
rules/why: Since powers add when exponentials multiply, ln turns a product into a sum. e squared times e cubed is e to the five, so its ln is five: two plus three, the ln of each factor, added.
rules/rule: The same holds for any positive numbers a and b: ln of a times b is ln a plus ln b.
rules/nums: ln two is about zero point six nine and ln three about one point one, so ln six is their sum, one point seven nine.
rules/nine: A power is a product of equal factors. Nine is three times three, so ln nine is ln three plus ln three: two ln three, about two point two.
rules/power: So for any power k, ln of a to the k is k times ln a: the power comes out in front.
quot/flip: Two times a half is one, and ln one is zero. So ln two plus ln a half is zero: ln of a half is minus ln two, about minus zero point six nine. One over a number flips the sign of its log.
quot/quot: Dividing by two is multiplying by a half. So ln of three halves is ln three plus ln a half, which is ln three minus ln two: about one point one minus zero point six nine, zero point four one.
quot/diff: The log of a quotient is the difference of the logs: ln of a over b is ln a minus ln b.
quot/small: So minus the log of a number below one is positive: minus ln of a half is zero point six nine. The smaller a number p, the bigger minus ln p: minus ln of a tenth is about two point three.
